newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Port Arthur killer tried to harm himself in cell.
newsitem.headline: Port Arthur killer tried to harm himself in cell.

text.p: Port Arthur mass murderer Martin Bryant tried to injure himself in his jail cell last month by swallowing a toothpaste tube, a prison official said on Friday.
The official declined to call the incident a suicide attempt, although it followed another incident last year when Bryant was found in his cell wrapping a bandage around his neck.
Bryant, 29, is serving a life sentence for shooting dead 35 people at the Tasmanian tourist spot of Port Arthur last April in modern Australia's worst mass killing.
"Martin Bryant attempted to swallow a toothpaste tube. He was not successful and medical attention was provided," said Doug Byers, manager of prison services in Tasmania state.
"It was removed by our medical staff and that was the end of the matter," Byers told Reuters from Tasmania's Risdon prison where Bryant is being held in a suicide-proof cell.
Bryant, described in his sentencing hearing as a pathetic social misfit who bore a grudge against society, is kept under constant camera surveillance in the prison's hospital wing.
He attempted to swallow the rolled-up toothpaste tube on February 1.

The tiny Port Arthur community is preparing to mark the first anniversary of the massacre on April 28 with a church service among the colonial-era convict ruins where Bryant unleashed his killing spree.
Prison authorities are trying gradually to introduce Bryant to the general prison population in Risdon, where a court has ordered he must spend the rest of his natural life.
For the first eight months after his arrest on April 29, he was kept in total isolation. Recently, he has been allowed to mix with other prisoners in the hospital wing, Byers said.
"Very gradual integration with other prisoners in the prison hospital has been put in place and it is working very successfully at this point in time," he said. "It's the first step."
